explanations: luna: The verse joins sealed hearts and hearing to “غِشَاوَةٌ” over sight, a sensory covering parallel to the section's closure and concealment. | terra: Hearts and hearing are sealed and sight bears a covering, making disbelief a closure of the very faculties by which guidance could enter.
luna: The section defines denial as covering truth; “وَلَا تَكْتُمُوا الْحَقَّ” names the act of hiding that truth.
terra: On the judgment day described here, no compensating equivalent is accepted and no help is given, setting the final limit on ransom as a means of release.

luna: The verse speaks of captives and “تُفَادُوهُمْ” while condemning their expulsion, directly activating the section's captive-and-ransom sense. | terra: The Israelites expel one another and make captives, then ransom those captives although the expulsion itself is forbidden; releasing a captive exposes the contradiction of first fastening the bond.
terra: The rejecters claim their hearts are wrapped, and the ayah answers that their disbelief has brought God’s curse; covering is both their stated stance and their refusal of belief.
terra: The repeated warning says no compensating equivalent will be accepted from any soul, reinforcing that the opportunity for costly release belongs before judgment.
luna: Those who conceal revealed proofs and guidance are condemned, a concrete case of the section's claim that deniers cover truth.
terra: The followers disown their leaders yet “وما هم بخارجين من النار”; severed human ties do not become release from the fire.

luna: “وَفِي الرِّقَابِ” names necks among the recipients of beloved wealth, in the same account of piety that includes patience through hardship. | terra: The definition of righteousness gathers giving beloved wealth to kin, orphans, and the needy, giving it “في الرقاب,” and steadfastness; it is the closest Quranic gathering of the section’s freed neck, feeding, and self-restraint.
terra: The fasting concession requires a fidyah consisting of feeding a needy person, so compensatory release from a bodily obligation itself takes the form of releasing another’s hunger.
terra: The pilgrim must wait “حتى يبلغ الهدي محله”; the هدي animal is led toward the point of release, while obstruction creates ransom, charity, or sacrifice in the same ayah.
terra: A wife may give compensation to obtain release when the couple fear they cannot keep God’s limits, turning payment into an exit from the marriage bond.
terra: The marriage knot may not be resolved before the waiting term reaches its end, using عقدة as a bond whose opening has a divinely set boundary.
terra: The marriage “knot” and the choice to forgo a financial half-share stand in one ayah; relinquishing a claim is placed at the boundary of a binding عقدة.
luna: The believer's firm handhold “لَا انفِصَامَ لَهَا” is an unbroken chosen bond, a boundary against treating every bond as a captive's restraint.
terra: Secret alms to the poor are better and God “يكفر عنكم” misdeeds; covering a gift and covering sins are merciful reversals of covering truth and closing wealth away.
terra: A debtor in hardship must be given respite, and remitting the debt as charity is better; a financial claim that could hold a person is deliberately loosened.

luna: The verse's “رِهَانٌ مَّقْبُوضَةٌ” is a pledge held as security, the very kind of locked pledge the section says can be opened. | terra: A journey without a scribe may require “فرهان مقبوضة,” collateral physically taken into possession; this is the Quranic legal scene behind the source section’s pledge locked until فك opens it.
luna: “وَتَكْتُمُونَ الْحَقَّ” explicitly pairs truth with concealment, clarifying the section's covering sense of disbelief.
terra: Even an earth-full of gold offered as ransom is not accepted from one who dies denying, setting the final limit on wealth’s power to release.
luna: “لَن تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتَّىٰ تُنفِقُوا مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ” gives the same costly generosity that frames freeing and feeding in the section.

luna: Believers are told to hold fast to God's rope together; this is a chosen bond that contrasts with the coercive neck-rope the section says should be undone. | terra: Holding together to God’s rope saves a formerly hostile people from the brink of fire; here a rope joins for rescue rather than fastening a neck for bondage.

luna: The section distinguishes restraining oneself from binding another; this verse praises those who “يَكْظِمُونَ الْغَيْظَ” and forgive people. | terra: The generous spend in ease and hardship, restrain anger, and pardon people; giving outwardly is paired with binding one’s own impulse rather than another person.

luna: The withheld wealth will “سَيُطَوَّقُونَ مَا بَخِلُوا بِهِ”; the neck becomes the miser's binding, reversing wealth used to free another. | terra: What people hoard from God’s bounty will be collared around them on resurrection, turning possessed wealth into the possessor’s neck-bond.
luna: The verse's covenant to disclose scripture and their subsequent concealment matches the section's covered truth, while showing the duty to uncover it.
terra: Believers ask God “كفر عنا سيئاتنا”; the same covering root becomes a plea for sins to be covered rather than truth.
terra: Those who consume orphans’ wealth consume fire into their bellies, turning wealth withheld from the vulnerable directly into fire within the withholder.
terra: The miserly conceal the bounty God gave them and urge others to miserliness; hidden provision and the punishment prepared for coverers meet in one ayah.

luna: Its expiation is “فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مُؤْمِنَةٍ,” a believing neck released, directly matching the section's manumission image. | terra: For an accidental killing, “تحرير رقبة مؤمنة” restores a believing human life through the release of another believing person represented by the neck.
terra: They again claim that their hearts are wrapped, but the ayah says God sealed them because of their disbelief, explicitly joining kufr to inner closure.

luna: The section names the h-d-y family and animal necks; 5:2 joins “الْهَدْيَ” with garlands worn by sacrificial animals, a concrete animal-and-neck meeting. | terra: The sacrificial animals and “القلائد” may not be violated; an animal led by the ه د ي family is marked at the neck by a garland, realizing the section’s link between leading and necks.
luna: The messenger clarifies much of scripture that people had concealed, directly opening the section's image of covered truth.
terra: All the earth’s wealth and as much again cannot ransom the disbeliever from the Day’s punishment, while the section spends wealth to free another before that day.

luna: Those in the Fire wish to leave but cannot, a specific closed boundary against the section's release from bonds. | terra: They wish to leave the fire but cannot leave it, an explicit denial of فك-like escape.

luna: Freeing a neck is one of this verse's expiations for a broken oath, alongside feeding or clothing the poor. | terra: The expiation of a binding oath is feeding or clothing ten poor people or “تحرير رقبة”; release from a verbal bond is enacted by feeding or releasing a human neck.
luna: The verse tests believers with game within reach of their hands and spears; this recalls the section's gazelle in a snare, although it does not say the game was trapped or escaped.
terra: A pilgrim who kills game must send an equivalent domestic animal as “هديا بالغ الكعبة”; the led offering and hunted animal meet in a compensatory neck-and-animal scene.
terra: The Kaaba, sacred month, sacrificial animals, and garlands are made supports for people; the led and neck-marked animal belongs to an ordered sacred boundary.

luna: The verse puts coverings on hearts and deafness in ears so people do not understand, a concrete obstruction of guidance like the section's covered sight. | terra: Coverings over hearts and heaviness in ears keep listeners from understanding, and even seeing every sign does not open belief.
terra: When people forget the reminder, the gates of everything are opened to them until sudden seizure overtakes their joy; abundance’s opening can itself become the mouth of a trap.

terra: The hypothetical sealing of hearing and hearts and removal of sight is followed by the question who besides God could restore them, defining both the closure and the sole power that can open it.
terra: Night covers Abraham before he examines the star and rejects what sets; darkness becomes the setting from which discernment of truth emerges.
luna: The verse accuses people of displaying some scripture while hiding much, a specific instance of the section's covering of truth.
luna: The section's root f-k-k is glossed as opening; the verse splits grain and date stone to begin growth, a related opening but not a bound creature's release.
terra: God expands the breast of one guided to submission but makes the breast of one led astray constricted and cramped, placing openness and closure on the two sides of guidance.
luna: “Heaven's gates will not be opened” for the arrogant, a specific boundary that mirrors the section's sealed fate.

luna: The verse gives the guilty a bed in Hell and coverings above them, a direct image of punishment covering them. | terra: Hell is a bed beneath the rejecters and coverings above them, a direct fire-enclosure on both sides.
luna: “يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ” gives night as a covering, matching the section's named dictionary sense of night as k-f-r because darkness conceals.

luna: The section opens a bound neck; this verse says the Messenger removes “الْأَغْلَالَ الَّتِي كَانَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ,” a direct release from shackles. | terra: The Messenger removes people’s burdens and “الأغلال التي كانت عليهم”; guidance here is an act of taking off bonds, the saving direction of the section’s opening motion.
terra: The battle command to strike above the necks is the violent boundary opposite “freeing a neck”; the shared bodily site carries contrary acts.
terra: If believers are mindful, God gives a criterion and “يكفر عنكم سيئاتكم”; covering sins accompanies discernment, opposite the covering that blocks truth.

luna: The verse explicitly discusses taking captives and the desire for ransom, giving the section's captive-and-ransom vocabulary a wartime boundary. | terra: The Prophet is warned against taking captives for the nearer world’s goods before the battle is decisively subdued, exposing material gain as a corrupt reason for fastening people.

luna: The Prophet addresses captives in his hands and promises them better than what was taken from them and forgiveness, a specific continuation of the captive scene. | terra: The Prophet is told to address captives in his hands: God may give them better than what was taken and forgive them, placing material loss and possible inward release together.
terra: Those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in God’s way are promised painful punishment, connecting closed-up wealth to its punitive return.
terra: The hoarded metal is heated in Hell and used to brand its owners, so possessed wealth becomes the instrument that takes possession of their bodies.

luna: “وَفِي الرِّقَابِ” makes freeing necks a specified destination for charity, as in the section's account of giving wealth to release the owned. | terra: The assigned uses of alms include “وفي الرقاب,” so wealth is expressly redirected from possession toward freeing possessed persons.
terra: The unjust soul would ransom itself with everything on earth when it sees punishment, but concealed regret cannot buy release.
terra: Joseph is drawn from the well as a boy and immediately hidden as merchandise, showing a child at the threshold of becoming property.
terra: Joseph is sold for a paltry price, completing 12:19’s movement from found child to possessed person and concretizing the source section’s child/slave overlap.

luna: The woman locks the doors before inviting Joseph, a specific closed-room scene that contrasts with the section's act of opening a binding. | terra: The doors are locked around Joseph, yet he restrains himself and refuses the invitation; external enclosure is answered by inward moral restraint.

luna: Joseph and the woman race to the door after the room is locked in 12:23, giving a particular attempted passage through the closed space. | terra: Joseph and the woman race to the door after the doors were locked in 12:23, making escape toward an opening the bodily continuation of his self-restraint.
luna: This verse also says night covers day, a repeated Quranic formulation of the covering sense the section assigns to night.

luna: The verse joins deniers, “الْأَغْلَالُ فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ,” and companions of the Fire, gathering the section's bound neck and closed-fire outcome. | terra: Those who cover their Lord’s truth have “الأغلال في أعناقهم” and are companions of the fire, joining disbelief, earth, neck-fetters, and final enclosure in one ayah.
terra: Those who do not answer their Lord would ransom themselves with the earth twice over, but their destination remains Hell.

luna: The guilty are seen bound together in shackles, a concrete restraint parallel to the section's neck and bond. | terra: The criminals are seen “مقرنين في الأصفاد,” coupled together in fetters, an exact collective scene of bodies made fast.

luna: Their garments are of tar and fire covers their faces, extending the section's binding image into punishment that covers the body. | terra: After the fetters of 14:49, fire covers their faces, joining bodily binding to the section’s reversal in which coverers are covered.
terra: The parable contrasts an owned slave who has no power with a person given good provision who spends it secretly and openly, joining human ownership, wealth, and release of provision.
terra: God seals the hearts, hearing, and sight of those who prefer the nearer life after belief, closing all three avenues of apprehension.
terra: Equivalent retaliation is permitted, yet patience is better; the harmed person’s restraint holds the self back from tightening harm on another.
terra: The command to be patient after 16:126 adds that such self-restraint comes only through God and must not collapse into grief or constriction over opponents.

luna: The deeds assigned “فِي عُنُقِهِ” are carried at the person's own neck, extending the section's neck-as-site-of-binding image to accountability. | terra: God fastens each person’s record of deeds to the neck, using the bodily site that represents the whole person for an obligation from which the person cannot detach himself.
terra: The object fastened to the neck in 17:13 becomes an open, outspread book that the person must read; opening exposes accountability rather than releasing it.

luna: “مَغْلُولَةً إِلَىٰ عُنُقِكَ” pictures one's own hand bound to one's neck, the section's inverse of freeing another person's neck. | terra: The miser is told not to make his hand “مغلولة إلى عنقك”; withheld wealth appears as the giver’s own hand chained to his neck.
luna: When the Quran is recited, a hidden barrier is placed between the reciter and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, a specific obstruction of guidance.
luna: Coverings on hearts and heaviness in ears block understanding of the recitation, extending the section's image of concealment to hearing.

luna: The section's dictionary form waṣīd means a threshold or door; 18:18 places the cave sleepers' dog at “بِالْوَصِيدِ.” | terra: The dog stretches its forelegs “بالوصيد,” using the section’s و ص د family for the cave’s threshold or entrance, the spatial edge from which the same root’s closing sense develops.

luna: The verse says to keep oneself patiently with the humble who call on God, closely matching the section's gloss of sabr as holding one's own self rather than another's neck. | terra: “واصبر نفسك” tells the Prophet to hold his own self with the people who call on God, an exact Quranic realization of the source definition “I restrained my self” for صبر.

luna: The Fire's canopies surround its occupants, a covering enclosure that makes visible the section's image of punishment closing around people. | terra: The unjust are surrounded by a fire whose walls encompass them, making rejection a place from which even a plea for relief brings scalding water.

luna: The verse describes coverings on hearts and deafness in ears after turning away, a specific barrier to guidance that matches the section's closure imagery. | terra: The one who turns from the reminder has coverings placed over the heart and heaviness in the ears, and cannot reach guidance while that closure persists.
luna: A fish slips away into the sea from the group's meal at the rock; this resembles the section's gazelle escaping a snare, though this verse does not describe a trap.

luna: The section glosses 90:2's root h-l-l as loosening a knot; Moses asks “وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِي,” applying that image to speech. | terra: Moses asks God “واحلل عقدة من لساني”; the section’s dictionary definition of حل as untying a knot becomes an explicit Quranic act that releases speech.

luna: This next verse gives the purpose of untying Moses' tongue-knot: that people understand his speech. | terra: “That they may understand my speech” states what the loosened tongue-knot of 20:27 makes possible: opening restores communication.
terra: The heavens and earth were a joined closure and God split them open, a cosmic instance of the section’s basic movement from tight joining to opening.

luna: When the condemned try to leave the Fire they are returned to it, making the section's shut fire an inescapable confinement. | terra: Whenever they try to leave the fire’s anguish, they are returned and told to taste the burning, repeating the no-exit boundary.
terra: People of means are told not to stop giving to kin, the needy, and emigrants, but to pardon and overlook; wealth and inward restraint jointly release another from deprivation.

luna: The section's released neck is funded from wealth; 24:33 tells owners to “فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ” when the enslaved seek a contract and to give them from God's wealth. | terra: Enslaved people seeking a manumission contract are to receive both the contract and some of the wealth God gave their owners, making wealth the means by which ownership’s bond is opened.

terra: The ayah places owned servants and children not yet at puberty side by side while distinguishing their privacy rules, clarifying the source section’s ولدان overlap between child and servant without collapsing the two.

luna: People are bound together in a narrow place of the Fire, an explicit enclosure joining bonds to the fire that closes in the section. | terra: They are thrown into a narrow place of the fire “مقرنين,” so confinement and binding reinforce one another spatially.
luna: Night is made “لِبَاسًا,” a garment that covers, matching the section's dictionary image of darkness covering what is beneath it.

luna: The verse says Hell encompasses the disbelievers, a specific image of the fire surrounding those whom the section says are shut over by it. | terra: Hell “لمحيطة بالكافرين,” explicitly enclosing the people who covered truth.

luna: On that Day punishment covers people from above and below, giving a bodily image of the section's “covered” condemned. | terra: The punishment covers them from above and from beneath their feet, giving the enclosure of 29:54 its vertical completeness.

luna: The verse says each attempt to leave the Fire is followed by return, giving the section's closed fire the concrete limit of no exit. | terra: Whenever the defiantly disobedient try to leave the fire, they are returned to it; desire for release cannot open the enclosure.
terra: God places fetters “في أعناق الذين كفروا,” again joining the covering of truth with a bond fixed at the neck.
terra: Whatever mercy God opens none can withhold, and whatever He withholds none can release afterward; opening and holding are set as opposite sovereign acts.
terra: Fetters are placed “في أعناقهم” up to their chins, making the neck-bond force the entire body into a fixed posture.
terra: Barriers before and behind the neck-fettered people of 36:8 cover them so they cannot see, adding visual enclosure to bodily bondage.

terra: The assembled wrongdoers and their objects of worship are commanded to be guided to the path of Hell, turning هدى into the leading of captives toward enclosure rather than guidance toward release.
luna: “We ransomed him with a great sacrifice” makes ransom the substitution that saves a person from death, a parallel to release by payment.
terra: The lasting gardens have their gates opened for the righteous, the welcoming reversal of heavenly gates barred to rejecters and fire closed over them.
luna: The verse says night is wrapped over day, a physical covering that makes the section's night-as-k-f-r dictionary sense perceptible.

luna: Canopies of fire lie above and beneath the punished, a second explicit enclosure around the inhabitants. | terra: Canopies of fire lie above and below them, rendering the punishment as layered cover.
terra: The one whose breast God opens to submission stands in divine light, while the hard-hearted face woe; inner opening reverses the sealed faculties of denial.
terra: Wrongdoers would offer all the earth and its like to ransom themselves when an unforeseen punishment appears; release sought only at enclosure comes too late.
terra: Hell’s gates are opened when the disbelievers arrive, showing that an opened door can admit a person into punishment rather than effect release.
terra: They are told to enter Hell’s gates and remain there, making the admission of 39:71 a permanent enclosure.

luna: The doors of the Garden are opened for its people, the direct opposite of the section's fire shut over its occupants. | terra: The mindful are led to the garden and find its gates opened, making opened entry the opposite destiny to the disbelievers’ enduring enclosure.
terra: Those who dispute God’s signs without warrant have every arrogant heart sealed; the same surah later shows such disputants dragged by neck-fetters in 40:71.

luna: “الْأَغْلَالُ فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ وَالسَّلَاسِلُ يُسْحَبُونَ” gives the neck, chains, and forced movement that reverse the section's act of release. | terra: The disputants are dragged with fetters “في أعناقهم” and chains, turning the neck that could have been freed into the point by which the whole person is hauled.

luna: After the collars and chains in 40:71, the verse says they are stoked in the Fire, completing the same punishment scene. | terra: Those dragged by neck-fetters in 40:71 are taken through boiling water and then burned in the fire, completing the bond’s destination.

luna: The speakers say their hearts are in coverings from the message, a direct image of people covering themselves against guidance. | terra: The rejecters themselves claim that their hearts are in coverings, their ears are deaf, and a veil stands between the two sides; their stance voices closure against the call.

terra: Even if the condemned endure patiently, the fire remains their lodging, and seeking restoration brings none; patience after enclosure no longer performs the saving self-restraint praised by the section.
terra: Repelling evil with what is better turns an enemy into a close ally, showing what the section’s inward restraint can release between people.
terra: Only those who are patient receive the transforming response of 41:34, explicitly naming the self-restraint that makes release of hostility possible.
terra: No fruit emerges from its sheath without God’s knowledge, showing the hidden thing opening from its plant-cover.
terra: Although a wrong may receive an equal answer, whoever pardons and repairs has a reward with God; this supplies the releasing act praised as patience and forgiveness in 42:43.
terra: Patience joined with forgiveness is called a matter of resolve, making self-restraint the condition for releasing another’s offense.

luna: A covering is placed on the sight of one who follows desire, and the verse asks who can guide him; this joins the section's cover and guidance images. | terra: A covering is put over the self-deifier’s sight and the ayah asks who can guide him afterward, explicitly linking covered perception to blocked guidance.
terra: Those who believe the truth have their misdeeds covered by God and their condition repaired, reversing the disbelievers’ covering in 47:1 before the neck-and-release law of 47:4.

luna: The section frees a neck; 47:4 places “فَضَرْبَ الرِّقَابِ” beside bonds and a choice of release or ransom, staging the same body, restraint, and release. | terra: The battle command moves from striking “الرقاب” to tightening the bond and then either gracious release or ransom, staging in one ayah the neck, the tightened tie, and its possible opening.
terra: The question whether hearts have “أقفالها” turns refusal to contemplate the Quran into an interior lock.
terra: The sacrificial animals are “معكوفا” and prevented from reaching their محل, staging a led animal held back before the place where its restriction would end.

terra: The believers are likened to a seed that strengthens into a crop delighting the sowers, while the same ayah says it enrages “الكفار”; cultivation and the disbelievers’ covering stand deliberately together.
terra: The people of the fire are told that whether they endure patiently or not is the same, marking the point at which صبر can no longer alter the bond’s outcome.

luna: “كُلُّ امْرِئٍ بِمَا كَسَبَ رَهِينٌ” makes a person a pledge for earned deeds, echoing the section's locked pledge and release vocabulary. | terra: After promising believing families reunion, the ayah says every person is “بما كسب رهين”; kinship cannot erase each person’s own pledged accountability.
terra: Date palms are “ذات الأكمام,” bearing sheathed fruit; the Quran directly presents the plant-container image used in the section to explain the covering family.
luna: This verse names the companions of the right, repeating the section's category for those whose acts include release and mercy.
luna: This verse names the companions of the left, the opposing group that the section places under its closed Fire.

luna: The section says the w-l-d dictionary form can mean a child or a slave; these serving youths fit the secondary sense, though the verse does not state that they are enslaved. | terra: Everlasting youths circulate in service, another Quranic use of ولدان that makes the source section’s child/servant lexical overlap visible.
luna: The passage again introduces the companions of the left, now as the people facing the punishment described in the following verses.
luna: Their punishment begins with scorching wind and boiling water, specific torment that expands the section's closed-fire scene.
luna: The left side has a shade of black smoke, a covering that turns the section's image of covering into punishment.
luna: The smoke is neither cool nor beneficial, specifying the hostile cover over the people of the left.
luna: The verse says they had lived in luxury, a concrete link between unspent abundance and the section's rich man boasting of amassed wealth.
luna: Their persistence in great sin explains why this group receives the punishment contrasted with the section's patient and merciful believers.
luna: They deny being raised after death, the same objection about becoming dust that the section cites with the neck-bound deniers in 13:5.
luna: The next verse extends that denial to their forefathers, completing the resurrection objection begun in 56:47.

luna: A wall divides two groups and has a door whose inside is mercy and outside punishment, a specific boundary that illuminates the section's closed fire. | terra: A wall with a gate divides mercy inside from punishment outside; this threshold shows that a door and enclosure can separate the two final companies.
luna: This continuation of the wall scene has those outside ask, “Were we not with you?”; the believers answer by naming their delay and doubt, specifying the boundary between the two groups.

luna: The verse says no ransom will be taken from the hypocrites and their refuge is fire, reversing the ransom that releases a captive and joining it to the section's fire. | terra: No ransom is accepted from hypocrites or disbelievers at the wall of 57:13, and the fire is their refuge; the opportunity to buy release has closed.

luna: In a plant-growth simile the verse uses “الْكُفَّارَ”; the section notes the k-f-r dictionary sense “farmer,” who covers seed with soil, though the verse's interpretation is disputed. | terra: The nearer life is vegetation after rain whose growth pleases “الكفار”; here the section’s secondary كافر, the farmer who covers seed, is present in a scene of growth that soon dries and breaks.

luna: For the wrong of zihar, 58:3 requires “فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ” before the spouses touch, making release a concrete act of repair. | terra: The one retracting ẓihār must perform “تحرير رقبة” before the couple touch, placing release of a neck before release from the speaker’s own binding utterance.
luna: If the neck-freeing expiation in 58:3 is unavailable, this verse prescribes fasting, a specific shift from freeing another to disciplining oneself.
terra: They believed and then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed; the sequence makes covering truth the cause of a further inability to understand.
terra: God has prescribed “تحلة أيمانكم,” the dissolution of oaths; the section’s حل of a knot becomes release from a binding utterance.
luna: Before the shackle order cited in 69:30, this verse gives a person his record in the right hand, the favorable side opposite the bound condemned person.
luna: The right-handed person says he expected to meet his account, giving the favorable side an explicit stance toward judgment.
luna: The right-handed person's outcome is a pleasing life, the counterpart to the fire and bonds described later in the same passage.
luna: The passage places that person in a high garden, completing the favorable outcome opposed to the closed Fire.
luna: Its fruit hangs near, a concrete detail of the ease given to the right-handed person before the passage turns to the left-handed one.
luna: They are told to eat and drink for what they sent ahead, linking deeds to the favorable judgment that contrasts with the section's bound deniers.
luna: The next person receives his record in the left hand and regrets it, directly continuing the division between the section's right and left companions.
luna: He wishes he had never received his record, specifying his rejection of the reckoning that the right-handed person welcomed.
luna: He wishes death had ended everything, continuing his regret before the binding order in 69:30.
luna: He says his wealth did not benefit him, a direct reversal of the section's wealthy man's boast and a lead into the punishment that follows.
luna: He says his authority is gone, completing the loss of power immediately before the order to shackle him.

luna: The order “خُذُوهُ فَغُلُّوهُ” turns bodily restraint onto the person who failed the section's ethic of faith and care. | terra: “خذوه فغلوه” orders that the unbelieving, ungenerous person be seized and fettered, the punitive reversal of taking hold of a bound person in order to free them.

luna: This verse carries 69:30's bound person into the blazing fire, completing the restraint-to-fire sequence that the section closes upon. | terra: This ayah casts the seized person of 69:30 into Hellfire, joining his fetter to the enclosing fire whose cause the following ayat disclose.

luna: The chain “ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُونَ ذِرَاعًا” extends 69:30's binding scene into a whole-body confinement; the section likewise moves from a bound neck to the shut fire. | terra: The command to insert him into a seventy-cubit chain completes the physical binding begun in 69:30.

luna: After the binding order in 69:30, this verse gives the failure of belief as its cause, paralleling the section's move from denial to punishment. | terra: His chain and fire are explained by the fact that he did not believe in God, matching the section’s movement from covering truth to being covered.

luna: After the binding order in 69:30, this verse says he did not urge feeding the poor, directly reversing the section's feeding and mercy. | terra: He also did not urge feeding the needy; the failure to loosen hunger for another returns as the chain imposed on himself in 69:30–32.
terra: After the condemned person failed to urge feeding the needy in 69:34, he has no food except foul discharge, reversing the feeding he would not support.

luna: A guilty person wishes to ransom himself from that Day's punishment with his children, reversing a ransom that frees a captive and showing that this release has a limit. | terra: The criminal wishes to ransom himself from that day’s punishment with his own children, reversing the section’s person who spends to release another.

luna: This continuation adds a spouse and brother to the family the guilty person would offer as ransom, widening the contrast with the section's actual release of a captive. | terra: The criminal would add his wife and brother to the child offered in 70:11, widening the attempted ransom through his closest relations.

luna: The imagined ransom expands to the clan that shelters him, carrying 70:11's impossible substitution into the social group. | terra: He would also offer the clan that sheltered him, completing the circle of human protection he tries unsuccessfully to exchange for release.

luna: He would offer everyone on earth to ransom himself, completing the escalating but unavailable release in 70:11–13. | terra: He would offer everyone on earth if it might save him, carrying the failed ransom of 70:11 to its absolute limit.

luna: The verse identifies the punishment as a blazing flame, specifying what the impossible ransom in 70:11 would avert. | terra: “كلا إنها لظى” closes the ransom attempt of 70:11–14: no offered substitute opens a way out of the blaze.
terra: The blaze of 70:15 calls the person who turned away, connecting inward refusal to the fire that will not accept his ransom.
terra: The person called by the blaze gathered wealth and shut it away, making his own act of enclosure the conduct answered by enclosing fire.
terra: God announces “أنكالا وجحيما,” fetters together with a blazing fire, the same conjunction of binding and final enclosure.

luna: “كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ” makes each soul a pledge held for its deeds, matching the section's dictionary image of unlocking a pledge. | terra: “كل نفس بما كسبت رهينة” makes every soul collateral for what it earns, directly activating the section’s locked pledge and asking what can effect its release.

luna: This verse exempts the companions of the right from the pledge in 74:38, paralleling the section's division between the saved and the people shut over by fire. | terra: The exception “إلا أصحاب اليمين” follows the pledged soul of 74:38 and names the same saved company that the surah places beyond the steep ascent and the freed neck.
luna: The companions in gardens ask about the condemned, a scene that gives the section's companions of the right a vantage opposite those confined in fire.
luna: This verse identifies the people in 74:40's inquiry as criminals, completing the division between the spared and the punished.

luna: The question “مَا سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ” asks how the criminals reached Saqar, connecting conduct to the section's closed-fire outcome. | terra: The question “What put you into Saqar?” connects the pledged soul and companions of the right in 74:38–39 to the fire whose causes include refusing to feed the needy in 74:44.
luna: The criminals say they did not feed the poor, directly reversing the section's food for the needy and captive.
luna: The criminals say they denied the Day of Judgment, giving a specific denial behind the section's transition from covering signs to fire.

luna: This is the guidance immediately preceding 76:4's chains; it recalls the section's two guided ways before the uphill act of release. | terra: God guides the human being to the way, after which one is grateful or coveringly ungrateful; 76:4 then turns that response into the boundary between guidance and fetters.

luna: Immediately after 76:3's guidance of the way, this verse prepares chains, shackles, and a blazing fire for deniers, reversing guidance's free passage. | terra: Immediately after the way is shown in 76:3, the rejecters receive chains, fetters, and a blaze; their response to guidance determines whether bondage or grateful action follows.

luna: The section lists kāfūr as the sheath around a palm blossom; the verse uses “كَافُورًا” in a drink, though that may be a different intended sense. | terra: The righteous drink a cup mixed with “كافورا”; this is the Quranic kāfūr drink term, not securely the source section’s palm-blossom sheath sense, but the shared dictionary form matters within the same surah’s captive, fetter, and serving-youth scenes.

luna: The section names an asir as someone to feed; 76:8 includes “أَسِيرًا” among those fed despite the givers' love of food. | terra: The righteous feed food they love to a poor person, an orphan, and “أسيرا”; care reaches the captive rather than tightening captivity.

luna: This continuation says the givers seek neither payment nor thanks, specifying the selfless motive behind 76:8's feeding of a captive. | terra: The feeders of the captive in 76:8 say they seek neither repayment nor thanks, identifying the inward restraint that keeps an act of release from becoming a new claim on its recipient.
luna: The givers fear a frowning, distressful Day, linking the section's compassionate acts to its final judgment and fire.
luna: This verse says God protects them from that day's evil, supplying the saving outcome after 76:8–10's charity and fear.

luna: After 76:8–11's feeding and fear of the Day, this verse says they are rewarded for patience, joining the section's feeding, self-restraint, and mercy. | terra: Because the righteous were patient, God rewards them with garden and silk; in the same surah the rejecters receive fetters, so self-restraint leads away from imposed restraint.

luna: The section says the w-l-d dictionary form can mean a child or a slave; this verse's serving youths fit that secondary sense, though it does not call them slaves. | terra: “ولدان مخلدون” circulate in service among the blessed; the Quranic serving youths activate the source section’s ولدان form at the border of child and servant.
luna: This command to be patient with the Lord's decree and resist the sinner develops the same sabr and self-restraint that the section places beside mercy.
luna: Night is made “لِبَاسًا,” the same explicit covering image as the section's dictionary sense of night as k-f-r.
luna: The section says sabr can mean holding one's own self; “وَنَهَى النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْهَوَىٰ” makes that self-restraint explicit.

luna: The verse says people's earnings have formed a coating over their hearts, a specific inward covering that develops the section's image of denial as concealment. | terra: What people earned has rusted over their hearts, presenting moral accumulation as a covering laid down from within.

luna: Those who covered are themselves screened from their Lord on the Day, directly enacting the section's claim that the coverers are covered. | terra: The rusted hearts of 83:14 are followed by being veiled from their Lord, making inner covering become final exclusion.

luna: This next verse says they enter the blazing Fire, completing 83:15's veil with the punishment that the section closes over its occupants. | terra: After the rust and veil of 83:14–15, they enter the blaze, completing the movement from self-made covering to punitive enclosure.

luna: The sealed pure drink is a covering that preserves a good gift, a useful counterpoint to the section's seal-like fire that confines its occupants. | terra: The righteous are given sealed pure drink, so closure preserves a gift rather than imprisoning people in punishment.

luna: The next verse identifies the drink's seal as musk, completing a beneficial seal that contrasts with the section's punishing closure. | terra: The seal of the drink in 83:25 is musk, specifying a fragrant, desirable sealing opposite the section’s punitive lid.
luna: The person given his record in his right hand receives the favorable side of the judgment, a repeated formulation of the section's division by right and left.
luna: This verse promises an easy reckoning to the right-handed person, specifying the judgment on the released side.
luna: He returns to his family joyful, completing the right-handed outcome before the passage turns to the person given his record behind his back.
luna: The other person receives his record behind his back, the sharp counterpart to the favorable right hand and the section's right/left division.
luna: He calls for destruction, continuing the regret of the person facing the section's closed-fire outcome.
luna: The person enters a blazing Fire, stating the punishment on the side opposite the section's companions of the right.
luna: He had been joyful among his family, a concrete account of his former ease before the judgment described here.
luna: He thought he would never return to God, directly paralleling the section's denial of resurrection before punishment.
luna: The verse says his Lord was watching him, answering the section's question about the person who thinks no one sees him.

luna: The verse rebukes failure to honor the orphan, directly reversing the section's orphan-care and mercy among the acts that pass the obstacle. | terra: Failure to honor the orphan begins a rebuke whose sequence ends in God’s incomparable binding, linking withheld care to the bond of 89:26.

luna: It rebukes failure to urge feeding the poor, the direct opposite of the section's feeding in hunger and care for the needy. | terra: The people do not urge one another to feed the needy, the same omission that explains the fettered person’s punishment in 69:34.

luna: The next charge is devouring inheritance greedily, specifying how abundance is consumed instead of used to free and feed others. | terra: They consume inheritance greedily, identifying acquisition without release as part of the conduct judged in the passage.

luna: The verse names intense love of wealth, a direct counterpoint to the section's spending wealth to release a neck. | terra: Their excessive love of wealth completes the withholding scene that culminates in the binding of 89:26.
luna: Hell is brought forth after the charges about the orphan, poor, and wealth, joining those failures to the section's closed Fire.
luna: The person regrets not sending good ahead for his afterlife, clarifying the lost use of wealth and action before Hell appears.
luna: The next verse says no one punishes as God does, sharpening the judgment that leads directly to the binding in 89:26.

luna: No one binds as God binds, a direct reversal of the section's freeing of a neck and a specific bond at the end of the orphan-and-wealth passage. | terra: “No one binds as His binding” gives the orphan-neglecting, wealth-loving passage its final bodily reversal: people who did not loosen need face an unmatched bond.

luna: The oath by night “إِذَا يَغْشَاهَا” pictures it covering the sun, a specific parallel to the section's night-as-concealment sense. | terra: Night “إذا يغشاها” covers the sun or the scene named by the pronoun, repeating the covering action behind the source section’s secondary night sense.

luna: The oath by night “إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ” gives the section's darkness-covering sense in a direct verbal image. | terra: The oath “والليل إذا يغشى” states that night covers, directly staging the dictionary explanation that night can be called kāfir because its darkness conceals.
terra: The warning of a blazing fire begins the outcome paired in this passage with denial and, on the opposite side, purification through giving wealth.
terra: The one who enters the blaze is the one who denied and turned away, joining covering truth to the fire announced in 92:14.
terra: The deeply mindful person is kept away from that fire, opening the passage’s opposite outcome.
terra: The person spared gives his wealth to purify himself, making wealth released outward the counterpart of the denier’s fire.

luna: The section's root f-k-k opens a trapped neck; 98:1 uses “مُّنفَكِّينَ” for those who would not desist or separate from denial until clear proof came. | terra: The Quran’s other occurrence of the section’s ف ك ك root says the disbelievers were not “منفكين” until the clear proof came; separation or release is placed beside the very covering of truth discussed in the section.
terra: Believers “تواصوا بالصبر” in the exact reciprocal wording used in 90:17, making shared counsel to self-restraint part of the way beyond bondage.

luna: The verse opens the passage cited by the section: a man gathers and counts wealth before the shut fire is described. | terra: The person destined for the closed fire of 104:8 accumulates wealth and keeps counting it, tying the enclosure to wealth kept under the counter’s control.

luna: The hoarder thinks his wealth will make him immortal, a direct setup for the section's closed fire and its contrast with wealth spent to free others. | terra: The wealth-counter thinks his wealth will make him immortal; this false confidence explains why accumulated wealth culminates in the closed fire of 104:8.

luna: The hoarder is cast into Hutama, beginning the fire passage completed by the section's cited shut-fire verses. | terra: The wealth-counter is thrown into the Crusher, beginning the punishment whose closed form is named in 104:8.
luna: The question asks what Hutama is, introducing the punishment whose closure the section draws out.
luna: Hutama is called God's kindled fire, specifying the fire in the section's closed-fire image. | terra: “The fire of God, kindled” identifies what 104:8 closes over them.

luna: The fire reaches hearts, adding its inward reach to the section's image of a fire that closes around its occupants. | terra: The fire rises over the hearts before it is described as closed over them, making enclosure penetrate the same inward place that truth can be covered.

luna: The same closing root named in the section appears in “عَلَيْهِم مُّؤْصَدَةٌ”; here the fire is shut upon the wealth-hoarder. | terra: The other Quranic “مؤصدة” says the fire is closed over the wealth-counter and slanderer, exactly repeating the section’s punitive lid.

luna: The extended pillars complete 104:8's sealed-fire image, giving a physical enclosure to the section's closed fire. | terra: “في عمد ممددة” supplies the extended columns of 104:8’s closure, giving the closed fire a structural image rather than merely naming confinement.
luna: The verse links denial of judgment to the conduct that follows, setting up a direct contrast with the section's faith and mercy.
luna: The denier repulses the orphan, a specific opposite to the section's care for the orphan as part of the uphill act.
luna: He does not urge feeding the poor, directly reversing the food and compassion that define the section's charitable scene.
luna: The preceding verse calls her the carrier of firewood, which makes the following rope around her neck a punishment tied to her own carrying.

luna: “فِي جِيدِهَا حَبْلٌ مِّن مَّسَدٍ” places a rope around a condemned woman's neck, the sharp reversal of freeing a neck. | terra: A rope of palm fibre is “في جيدها,” staging the section’s dictionary scene of a rope thrown around the neck rather than the rope being removed.

luna: “فِي الْعُقَدِ” names knots as a source of harm, a specific counter-image to the section's loosening of a knot to release a captive. | terra: The blowers act “في العقد,” a scene of knots being worked for harm rather than the saving untying named by the section.
